items.title: Verstappen takes Red Bull's first pole of 2026, 0.298s clear of Hamilton
items.summary: Max Verstappen was quickest in all three segments and set 1m35.130s in Q3, 0.298s ahead of Lewis Hamilton, with Isack Hadjar third on track and Kimi Antonelli fourth. The Race notes it is the first pole for a non-Mercedes-powered car this season and the first Verstappen-Hamilton front row since Abu Dhabi 2021. Mercedes' best was fourth and eighth.
items.why_it_matters: Red Bull's pace is a genuine change in the 2026 order, though Friday and Sunday running (and Pirelli's tyre-stress warnings) may differ from one lap. Mercedes' qualifying deficit is a key race-day question.

items.title: Hadjar, Colapinto and Lindblad serve power-unit/collision grid penalties
items.summary: Official starting grid: Verstappen, Hamilton, Antonelli, Leclerc, Norris, Piastri, Russell, with Hadjar dropped from third to eighth by a five-place penalty for a seventh internal combustion engine. Colapinto (five-place carry-over from the Baku collision) and Lindblad (new power-unit components) occupy the last two grid slots, 21st and 22nd.
items.why_it_matters: Russell's eighth on track becomes seventh on the grid. Use the official grid, not the qualifying classification, for starting positions and recovery-drive narratives.

items.title: Mercedes' seven-part upgrade package does not deliver in qualifying
items.summary: FIA Document 12 lists 14 declared upgrade items, seven of them Mercedes'. Antonelli was fastest in FP3 but qualified fourth and Russell eighth; Russell was left 'perplexed' and expects a different story in the race, while The Race calls it Mercedes' worst qualifying since Hungary.
items.why_it_matters: Declared items are not a lap-time guarantee; the gap between Friday/FP3 form and qualifying is the open question for Sunday.

items.title: FIA declares a Heat Hazard for Sunday's race
items.summary: FIA Document 3 declares a Heat Hazard under Article B1.5.10 because the official forecast Heat Index exceeds 31.0 degrees Celsius at some point during the Race. The venue is Sepang, with Sunday's start at 15:00 MYT / 10:00 Tallinn.
items.why_it_matters: This is an official declaration, not a generic weather warning. Do not equate Heat Index with ambient temperature or infer cooling-system requirements from temperature alone.

items.title: Pirelli details Sepang surface work before its return
items.summary: Pirelli reports that Sepang's Turns 6–12 section was resurfaced in 2023, with further work around Turn 9, and that additional levelling and cleaning took place from early September 2026. Engineers still assess the overall surface characteristics as similar to 2017. The event poster rates tyre stress and abrasion 4/5, nominates C2/C3/C4 and estimates 22.5 seconds pit-stop loss.
items.why_it_matters: Do not describe the circuit as untouched since 2017: sections have been resurfaced and levelled. Keep that work distinct from Pirelli's current assessment of similar overall surface characteristics; tyre behaviour for this generation remains unknown until practice.
